problem: A leftover authoring artefact is printed in the middle of the worked example: "dry run: {'head': [], 'rows': []}". Students will see an empty table skeleton and a raw object instead of a solution step.
fix: Delete the line entirely. The example should run step 1 to step 7 and then the answer sentence.

problem: Producer gas LHV is given as "about 5–6 MJ/kg". Air-blown producer gas is normally quoted per normal cubic metre, about 4–6 MJ/Nm³; because its density is roughly 1.1–1.2 kg/Nm³, the value per kg is only about 4–4.5 MJ/kg. The stated figure overstates energy per kg by about a third.
fix: Producer gas is mostly N2, CO and H2 with LHV about 4–6 MJ/Nm³ (roughly 4 MJ/kg), best for stationary engines.

problem: The single root note "lower CO2 per MJ" is attached to all six fuels. On a per-megajoule basis biodiesel is about the same as, or slightly above, petroleum diesel (about 0.074 vs 0.072 kg CO2/MJ); its benefit is biogenic carbon and well-to-wheel accounting, not tailpipe CO2 per MJ. A student may carry away a wrong generalisation.
fix: Change the root note to something universally true, for example "lower carbon or cleaner combustion", and state the CO2-per-MJ benefit only for CNG, LPG and hydrogen.

problem: "Its supply is tied to refinery output" is only partly true. A large share of LPG comes from natural gas processing and fractionation of natural gas liquids, not from crude oil refineries alone.
fix: Say: its supply is tied to refinery and natural gas processing output.

problem: DME is grouped as a liquid fuel, but at ambient temperature and pressure it is a gas; it is carried as a liquid only under about 5 bar pressure. On its own the tree implies DME is a liquid like ethanol.
fix: Label the DME node "gas at 1 atm, stored liquid near 5 bar" so the storage basis is visible.
